subject: Mobile Development
title: Apple vs. FBI: The San Bernardino Case
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Apple vs. FBI: The San Bernardino Case.

hook.text: After a 2015 terror attack, the FBI asked Apple to unlock the shooter's iPhone. Apple refused.

buildup.text: Apple argued that creating a backdoor for one phone would endanger all iPhones everywhere.

discovery.text: The FBI eventually paid a third party over $1 million to crack the phone without Apple's help.

twist.text: The phone contained nothing useful. The entire legal battle was fought over an empty device.

climax.text: The case set a precedent: tech companies can resist government demands for encryption backdoors.

punchline.text: Apple chose user security over government demands.

quiz.question: Why did Apple refuse to unlock the San Bernardino iPhone?
options: A backdoor for one phone would endanger all iPhones
